title: Tension
body: Tension is the macroscopic net result of the forces that infinitesimal segments of a string, cable, chain, or similar system exert on each other in response to an external force.
caution: Tension is uniform only for an ideal string (negligible mass, does not stretch). In a string with nonnegligible mass, tension may differ from point to point.
ced_evidence: 2.3.A.3: "Tension is the macroscopic net result of forces that infinitesimal segments of a string, cable, chain, or similar system exert on each other in response to an external force."

title: Net force and translational equilibrium
caution: Net force is the vector sum of all forces exerted on the system. Translational equilibrium is the case where that sum is zero, so velocity stays constant. Forces can balance in one dimension and not in another, and velocity changes only along the unbalanced direction.
ced_evidence: 2.4.A.1 "The net force on a system is the vector sum of all forces exerted on the system"; 2.4.A.2 "Translational equilibrium is the configuration of forces such that the net force exerted on a system is zero"

title: Gravitational field strength
caution: M is the mass of the system creating the field and m is the test object. When gravity is the only force on an object, its acceleration in m/s^2 is numerically equal to g in N/kg at that location.
ced_evidence: 2.6.A.2.i "The magnitude of the gravitational field created by a system of mass M at a point in space is equal to the ratio of the gravitational force... to the mass of the test object"; 2.6.A.2.ii

title: Solving motion under a resistive force
body: Steps for finding velocity, position, and acceleration of an object under a resistive force such as F_r = -kv.

items.meaning: Apply Newton's second law to the object with the resistive force, which gives a differential equation for velocity.
Use separation of variables to solve for the velocity.
Integrate over the proper limits of integration.
With velocity known as a function of time, use initial conditions and calculus to get position or acceleration.
Check the result: for F_r = -kv, position, velocity, and acceleration are exponential in time, with asymptotes set by the initial conditions and the forces exerted.
For terminal velocity, the maximum speed under a constant force and an opposing resistive force, set the net force equal to zero.

ced_evidence: 2.9.A.2 "results in a differential equation for velocity"; 2.9.A.2.i "method of separation of variables"; 2.9.A.3 "The terminal condition is reached when the net force exerted on the object is zero"

title: Sources of centripetal force in named cases
body: In each named case, identify which force or force components supply the centripetal acceleration toward the center of the circular path.

items.label: Top of a vertical loop (minimum speed)
items.meaning: Gravity is the only force causing the centripetal acceleration, which gives v = \sqrt{gr}.

items.label: Banked surface
items.meaning: Components of the static friction force and the normal force contribute to the net force producing centripetal acceleration.

items.label: Conical pendulum
items.meaning: A component of the tension contributes to the net force producing centripetal acceleration.

items.label: Satellite in circular orbit
items.meaning: Gravitational attraction alone causes the centripetal acceleration.

caution: Centripetal force is not a separate force on a free-body diagram. Name the actual forces, or their components, that point toward the center.
ced_evidence: 2.10.A.2 "Centripetal acceleration can result from a single force, more than one force, or components of forces"; 2.10.A.2.i-iii; 2.10.B.1
